text.p: Typhoon Tina has top winds of 110 mph and is currently south of Japan, moving north northwest. Tina may strengthen to 120 mph and should pass just west of Okinawa in about 36 hours, resulting in storm surge flooding, wind damage, and flooding rain. Tina may then weaken slightly but should still be quite strong as it tracks toward Cheju, just south of southern Korea, reaching the island in about 72 hours. Damage will likely result in Cheju into southern Korea as Tina moves in by late Friday night, local time.
Heavy rain and thunderstorms in Bangladesh the next few days may lead to further flooding resulting in crop and property damage.
In Germany and Poland, flood cleanup continues on the Oder River. A drier, warmer pattern will be favorable.
In the USA Southwest and Rockies, thunderstorms have caused local flash flooding in portions of the region and additional storms may add to flooding during the next few days.

Hurricane Guillermo has top wind of 160 mph but is over open waters in the eastern Pacific about 975 miles southwest of the southern tip of Baja, moving west. This system is a major threat to shipping. It is still well east of Hawaii but will be closely monitored over the next few days.
